messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477()` tests the parsing of a pattern string that contains escaped single quotes: `"it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!"`. The test creates an `ExtendedMessageFormat` instance with this pattern and a custom `registry`. The issue report indicates that using `ExtendedMessageFormat` with a custom format registry and patterns containing single quotes leads to an `OutOfMemoryError`.

From the constructors of `ExtendedMessageFormat`, the constructor with `(String pattern, Map registry)` calls the constructor `(String pattern, Locale locale, Map registry)` which saves the `registry` and calls `applyPattern(pattern)` to parse the pattern.

The `applyPattern` method shows distinct handling depending on whether a custom `registry` is present. With a custom registry, the method parses the pattern character by character, handling formatting elements and quoted strings via the method `appendQuotedString`.

The `appendQuotedString` method is key for handling quoted substrings in the pattern. It scans the pattern starting at the current parse position, appending characters to a buffer until it encounters a close quote character. It also handles escaped quotes (two consecutive quotes) by appending a single quote character and advancing the position.

The failing test's pattern has multiple consecutive single quotes (e.g., `''` in `it''s`). The `appendQuotedString` method relies on detecting the end of a quoted string by a quote character and also specifically handles escaped quotes by advancing the parse position over double quotes.

However, the infinite loop or `OutOfMemoryError` likely arises if the pattern parsing's quotation handling loops excessively when encountering escaped quotes together with the custom format registry logic. Specifically, in `appendQuotedString`, when it detects an escaped quote sequence starting at `i`, it appends a quote and sets the parse position to `i + ESCAPED_QUOTE.length()`, updating `lastHold` accordingly. But the outer `while` loop in `applyPattern` calls `appendQuotedString` whenever it sees a quote character, which may cause repetitive parsing of the same quoted substring without properly advancing the parse position in all cases.

In sum, the bug seems to be a parsing loop in `applyPattern` combined with incorrect or incomplete parse position advancement in `appendQuotedString` when handling escaped single quotes inside quoted strings, leading to repeated infinite parsing and unbounded memory use — hence the `OutOfMemoryError` in the presence of single quotes with a custom format registry.

No recent bug reports provide contradictory evidence, so the root cause is likely this interplay between `applyPattern` and `appendQuotedString` in the extended message format parsing code.

This matches the issue report's description of the problem occurring specifically with custom registries and single-quote-containing patterns.

Next, I suggest checking and fixing the logic in `applyPattern` and `appendQuotedString` to correctly handle position advancement and quoting cases to avoid infinite loops and memory leaks.

Methods to be fixed:
- `ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)`
- `ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String,java.text.ParsePosition,java.lang.StringBuffer,boolean)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
